correctness.rationale: Using the Fano nonline-triple Coxeter presentation, the 42-edge compatibility graph has 84 seven-cliques and no eight-clique; independently re-enumerated both exhaustive sets in a separate Python checker. The sources provide two distinct checkers (Fano maximal-clique and seven-cycle/star direct k-clique enumeration) and explicit 28 distance-three sphere cores F_v, each six matching edges. Exact complete optimal set equals 84 F_v+vw. Independent computation verified pairwise exact-exchange histogram: k1=84,k4=168,k5=672,k6=1470,k7=1092 and no k2/k3. Source verifiers reconstruct 56 triangles in J4, a 56-vertex cubic triangle intersection graph, a complete fixed bijection with Sage Klein3RegularGraph adjacency, and BFS shells (1,4,8,16,22,26,7), and at-most-four connectivity diameter4. The independent computation covered optimality and histogram, not separately the full named isomorphism certificate.
residual_risks: An earlier Coxeter–Klein construction in strong-edge terminology may conceal this precise matching-reconfiguration representation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Dejter had constructed the same Coxeter-to-Klein graph through oriented seven-cycle zipping; the connection itself is prior. Joos–Rautenbach–Sasse give general lower bounds for subcubic induced matchings, not the 84 optima or associated exact reconfiguration graph. Stronger generic/family theorems were compared by their actual implications rather than title alone; these listed results do not give the particular new invariant.
